raw_response:
I’m not going to spread myself too thin this year. I only have 7.8 mu, and some people in the family work outside, so the land still has to be managed in a steady way, not too fancy. Same as the last few years, I’ll keep most of the land in wheat-maize because that is the safe way here. Wheat gives a steady harvest, and maize follows right after, so even if one side is weak, the other can still help. I’ll leave 2.8 mu for cotton. Cotton can make money if the price is decent, but it takes more watching and more picking, so I won’t put too much land into it.

For wheat, I’ll plant around early October, about 5 mu. I usually follow what people nearby do. I’ll use improved seed from the local dealer, but not the expensive kind. Before sowing I’ll put some base fertilizer, mostly compound fertilizer with a bit of urea. I don’t dare cut fertilizer too much because if wheat turns yellow later, yield falls fast. But I also can’t spend too much cash at once, so I’ll split it: some at sowing, some at jointing. With well water, I’ll probably irrigate three times if the year is normal: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing, once around grain filling if needed. For maize on the same 5 mu, I’ll seed it right after wheat harvest in mid-June. That window is tight, so I won’t do heavy tillage, just quick rotary tillage or direct planting if I can get help from a machine. Maize also needs fertilizer, but I won’t overdo it. I’ll put some at planting and one topdress around the big bell stage. Usually one or two irrigations are enough if rain is not too bad.

Cotton is different. I’ll keep it on 2.8 mu, the fields that are a bit easier for me to watch. Cotton needs more labor, especially later for picking, so I keep the area limited. I’ll plant in mid-April. I’ll use decent local hybrid seed, not the highest-priced one. Fertilizer will be moderate, a bit at planting and another time later. If insects show up, especially aphids or bollworms, I’ll spray; if not, I won’t waste money. Cotton can make money, but if I put too much cash into it and the price is poor, that money is stuck. So this year I’ll farm it carefully, not aggressively.
